semantic_findings.result: CompleteOddFiber has no conditions on the raw output r beyond equality to original Agent8.stepWord. It requires all source conditions literally on q: odd exact length, symmetry, bounds below 19, positive outer coefficient, even actual center, and final scan carry zero.

Every digit in scan is a remainder below ten. A source word of length 2*m+1 gives exactly that many scan digits. Final carry zero makes original normalization equal this digit list. Splitting it into two equal halves and one digit, then applying original pair, yields an encoded target with m Fin19 symbols and one Fin10 center. No source symmetry or coefficient bound is needed for this stronger range lemma.

targetHalf and targetCenter are computable for every raw list, including malformed ones. The exact reconstruction equality and half-length guard prevent modulo reduction or missing-entry defaults from admitting a different target.

When the guard is true, fullOddPreimages_membership is definitionally the literal CompleteOddFiber predicate. When false, any alleged literal fiber would have an encoded actual output by OddOutputRange; exact decoder identities then force the guard true, a contradiction. Thus rejected target lists have genuinely empty fibers.

The accepted branch inherits fullOddPreimages Nodup and its bound; the rejected branch is empty. Every m has an explicitly encoded sharp target whose universal enumerator equals sharpFamily and attains (fib (m+1)+1)/2. The theorem quantifies over all r and all q without a target-shape hypothesis.

All 25 singleton target coefficients 0..24 were checked directly. Short, long, asymmetric, odd-center, out-of-alphabet, modulo-aliasing, empty and zero-source-head cases were checked. The exact fiber for [11,12,11] is [[5,16,5]], distinguishing source center16, normalized digit6 and paired target center12. A nonsymmetric source [100,0,0] controls the stronger unbounded output-range statement.
